title: Analysis of PFNA closed reduction and internal fixation combined with extracorporeal shock wave therapy for intertrochanteric femoral fractures

summary.en: The intervention group demonstrated shorter times to full weight-bearing and fracture healing than the control group (both P < 0.001). Compared with preoperative values, HHS scores increased at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively in both groups, with higher scores in the intervention group (P < 0.001, P < 0.001, and P = 0.004, respectively). Compared with preoperative values, VAS scores decreased at 1, 3, and 6 months in both groups, with lower scores in the intervention group (all P < 0.001).

title: Exercise interventions for glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a three-level meta-analysis with exploratory machine-learning analysis

summary.en: Exercise significantly improved glycemic control (g = -0.738, 95% CI -1.046 to -0.430, p < 0.001), corresponding to reductions of 0.52% in HbA1c, 1.13 mmol/L in fasting glucose and 1.87 mmol/L in 2-hour postprandial glucose. Heterogeneity was substantial (I2 = 86.0%, tau2 = 1.125; 95% prediction interval -2.98 to 1.50). All three outcomes improved significantly, whereas between-modality differences were not significant (p = 0.544).

title: MobilityAPP: A Randomized Controlled Trial Evaluating Gait-Focused Physiotherapy in Parkinson Disease and Atypical Parkinsonian Syndromes

summary.en: Of 167 patients screened, 160 were included (mean age 67.4, 51.2% female) and 151 completed the study per protocol (85 with APD, 66 with PD; 76 GPT, 75 SPT). GPT was comparable to SPT in improving self-paced gait speed (95% CI -0.04 to 0.04; p = 0.949). However, positive changes in daily-life mobility metrics were observed that favored the GPT intervention.

title: Progressive Wuqinxi Cardiac Rehabilitation Based on Dual-Heart Theory in Patients with Chronic Heart Failure

summary.en: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is associated with declining exercise tolerance, impaired quality of life, and high readmission rates despite guideline-directed therapy. Cardiac rehabilitation is recommended, yet scalable models that integrate mind-body regulation with somatic cardiac recovery remain limited in China. Grounded in the Dual-Heart Theory (coordination of the somatic heart and the mind/spirit), we developed a 12-week Progressive Wuqinxi cardiac rehabilitation program and tested it in a randomized controlled trial.

title: Effect of a theory-informed multicomponent exercise program on cognitive function and other health outcomes among older adults with mild cognitive impairment: the MIND-STEP randomized controlled trial
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

summary.en: Compared with unstructured usual care, the MIND-STEP program significantly improved MoCA-B at 12 weeks (mean difference = 2.78; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.88 to 3.68, p < 0.001, standardized mean difference = 1.23; 95% CI: 0.83 to 1.63), with benefits observed at 6 weeks and maintained at 24 weeks. Intrinsic capacity, physical performance, depressive symptoms and sleep quality also improved. DISCUSSION: The MIND-STEP program improved cognition and overall health in nursing-home residents with MCI compared with unstructured usual care, supporting structured exercise and behavior-change strategies in routine nursing-home care.

title: Structured exercise is associated with improved functional outcomes in myopathies and related neuromuscular diseases: a systematic review and exploratory dose-response meta-analysis

summary.en: twenty-two reports representing 21 independent studies and 614 participants across the reported study cohorts were included in the systematic review. The corrected quantitative data set comprised 21 valid effects from 13 independent trials; 403 participants contributed data to the primary analysis. The primary analysis found a positive pooled effect (g = 0.567, 95% CI 0.268 to 0.867; p = 0.001; I 2 = 44.8%), although the 95% prediction interval crossed zero (-0.243 to 1.377).

title: Lee Silverman Voice Treatment-BIG Group Therapy Effects on Motor Function, Occupational Performance, Activities of Daily Living, Depression, and Quality of Life in Patients With Stroke
journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research

summary.en: BACKGROUND This study investigated the additional effects of Lee Silverman Voice Treatment-BIG (LSVT-BIG) group therapy when combined with conventional rehabilitation on motor function in patients with stroke. Occupational performance, activities of daily living, depression, and quality of life were secondary outcomes. MATERIAL AND METHODS Sixteen patients were randomly assigned to an experimental (n=8) or control group (n=8).

title: Effect of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation on postoperative liver injury in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy: a phase II clinical randomized trial

summary.en: Perioperative liver injury is a common complication following partial hepatectomy in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. Preclinical studies have shown that transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has hepatoprotective effects, but clinical evidence remains limited. This study is a phase II, prospective, double-blind, randomized trial involving 140 patients undergoing partial hepatectomy, in which the active-taVNS group received 60-minute stimulation sessions at four time points: during the first hepatic pedicle clamping, after extubation in the post-anesthesia care unit, and on postoperative days 1 and 2 between 6:00 AM and 7:00 AM.

title: Microdosing in Plyometric Training: Effects of Frequency Distribution on Physical Performance in Team-Sport Athletes-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
journal: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports

summary.en: How weekly plyometric jump training (PJT) should be distributed remains uncertain because frequency and volume often covary. This systematic review and meta-analysis compared higher- versus lower-frequency PJT in healthy team-sport athletes, with matched or closely matched cumulative/average weekly planned volume as the primary comparison and unequal-volume comparisons analyzed separately. Twelve studies were included, and 11 contributed quantitative data.

title: Rehabilitation Strategies for Upper Limb Function After Breast Cancer Treatment, with and Without Lymphedema: The Potential of Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation - A Systematic Review

summary.en: Six trials (366 women) were included: three enrolled women with confirmed BCRL and three women without BCRL. PNF was mostly part of multimodal programs, but the between-group contrast isolated PNF in four trials. In BCRL trials, limb volume decreased in all groups, with no consistent advantage of PNF over active comparators.

title: Efficacy of laser therapy for subacromial impingement syndrome: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials

summary.en: The study compared the effects of high-intensity laser therapy (HILT), low-level laser therapy (LLLT), and conventional physical therapy (CPT) on shoulder pain and function in patients with subacromial impingement syndrome (SIS). Eight databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The outcomes in this study were pain (visual analogue scale, VAS) and shoulder function (Shoulder Pain and Disability Index, SPADI).
